Konstantynow Lodzki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Konstantynów Łódzki, Poland

Demolished. Konstantynów Łódzki's Jewish community was established in 1832, numbering 1,091 people (19.5 percent of the town) by 1897. On December 22, 1939, the Germans expelled all Jewish inhabitants to Główno. This cemetery, likely established alongside the kehilla in 1832, was significantly damaged during WWII, with some matzevot used to harden roads and sidewalks in front of Gestapo headquarters, now the town library; according to a local resident, surviving postwar matzevot were gradually destroyed and stolen by residents. A commemorative plaque was erected around 2013, and as of 2021 a further memorial project by Jews from the town remained unimplemented.
